## Ethics Statement

This work studies the optimization of agent harnesses with existing language models and benchmark datasets spanning text tasks, mathematical reasoning, code generation, and simulated scientific interaction. The experiments evaluate model outputs and executable programs within the specified benchmark protocols; they do not involve recruiting human participants or deploying systems in real-world decision-making. Diagnosis, legal, and chemical outputs are used only as benchmark predictions. We are not aware of specific ethical concerns arising from the experiments reported in this study.

## Reproducibility Statement

The main text and appendices detail the MESH-Harness design and experiments.

Algorithm 4 and Section 4 specify the MESH-Harness procedure, while Appendix A provides the theoretical analysis and Appendix B expands the optimization loop, composition selection, and module refresh procedures. Section 5.1 identifies the models, benchmarks, baselines, and evaluation protocol. Appendix C details the data splits, retrieval resources, memory boundaries, search hyperparameters, execution limits, scoring rules, and cost accounting. Appendix D describes the selected harnesses and their task-specific control flow. All comparisons use the shared task splits and scoring protocols described in the paper. Final harnesses are selected on validation data and frozen before testing; reported test scores average three executions of each frozen harness. The models, benchmarks, and retrieval sources are identified and cited in the manuscript.
